plain Markdown viewer, on GitHub without Mermaid support, or in a rendered docs
artefact cannot see the graph and cannot easily tell the shape of the shipped
storylines. Rendering it to a portable SVG in a documented docs step and
linking it from `docs/main-street/storylines.md` makes the graph viewable
everywhere, without requiring a Mermaid-aware renderer.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — need to see the storyline shape at a
  glance in the docs, without installing Mermaid tooling.
  - *"As a content designer, I want the storyline graph shown as an image in the
    docs, so I can inspect the shipped chains without a Mermaid renderer."*
- **Developers / reviewers** — need the rendered graph to stay in sync with the
  committed Mermaid source so reviews trust the picture.
  - *"As a reviewer, I want a drift guard between the rendered image and the
    committed `.mmd`, so a stale graph cannot be merged."*
- **Docs build / maintainers** — need a deterministic, reproducible render step
  with no manual copy-paste.
  - *"As a maintainer, I want one documented command that regenerates the
    rendered graph, so the artefact is reproducible."*

## Acceptance Criteria

> **Finalised** per producer answers to Q1–Q3 (2026-10-07): minimal npm render
> step (A); reuse Playwright + `mermaid` devDependency (B); SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift
> guard (A).

1. **Rendered artefact** — a rendered graph image (`docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg`)
   is committed under `docs/main-street/` and is viewable without a
   Mermaid-aware renderer (SVG preferred; PNG only if SVG cannot be emitted).
2. **Reproducible render step** — a documented npm script renders the committed
   `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` into the committed image
   deterministically (no RNG, timestamp or wall-clock input; byte-identical on
   re-run). The renderer is a **devDependency only** and does not enter the
   game bundle.
3. **Doc link** — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` embeds or links the rendered
   image (in §7.2 "The shipped graph" and/or §11 "Related documents"),
   documenting the new regeneration command in the §5 tooling table.
4. **Drift guard (validation)** — an automated test/check fails when the
   committed rendered SVG drifts from the committed `.mmd`. The existing
   `.mmd`-vs-`src/card-data.csv` `--check` guard must continue to pass.
5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No mandatory new runtime dependency for the game** — any renderer
  dependency is a **devDependency** only and must not enter the game bundle.
  Reuse the already-installed `playwright` Chromium (no second Chromium
  download).
- **Determinism** — the render must be reproducible from the committed `.mmd`;
  no timestamps/ids embedded in the output that would churn on every run.
- **Mermaid is the source of truth** — the `.mmd` remains the generated
  artefact of record; the image is derived, never hand-edited.
- **Licensing** — any added dependency must be permissively licensed (MIT,
  Apache-2.0, CC0). The `mermaid` package is MIT.
- **Scope** — do not redesign the graph content or the storyline model, and do
  not build a full static docs site (deferred to `MS-0MUYK064P0032374`). This
  item only renders and links the existing graph.

## Existing state (repo research)

  choice cards as diamonds, plain incidents as rounded rectangles, cycle edges
  as `==>`.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` — generator/CLI: `--format mermaid|json`,

- `src/scripts/storyline-graph-cli.ts` — CLI entry; npm script

- `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts` — asserts the committed `.mmd`

- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — canonical doc. §5 Tooling, §7.2 shipped

- `package.json` — scripts include `storylines:graph`, `validate:storylines`;
  devDependencies already include `playwright`, `sharp`, `vite-node`/`vite`,
  `vitest`. **No `mermaid`, `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli`, `puppeteer` or docs site
  generator (mkdocs/docusaurus) is present anywhere in the repo or `core/`.**
- **There is no "docs build"** in `tce-main-street`: `docs/` is plain Markdown,
  there is no docs npm script, no mkdocs/docusaurus config, and no docs-site CI
  workflow. The only Pages workflow (`core/.github/workflows/deploy.yml`)
  deploys the game bundle, not these docs.

## Desired change

1. **Render** the committed `.mmd` into a portable SVG via a documented,

   Chromium and the `mermaid` JS package (devDependency).

### Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

    toolchain the repo does not otherwise use.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (A)** — minimal npm render step.

# Intake Brief: Easy editing of tutorial text

**Recreated from the core work item `CG-0MUAVHX1D002J8HH`** in the Tableau-Card-Engine store. The Main Street game — and therefore all tutorial copy — now lives in this repository (`tce-main-street`), so this item is the game-repo record of the same change. Cross-repo pointer: `CG-0MUAVHX1D002J8HH`; implementation commit `beeed4d` on `dev`.

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Feature**

## Problem statement

Main Street tutorial copy is already externalised out of gameplay code, but it lives in a **TypeScript source module** (`src/i18n/tutorial-en.ts`) whose values are wrapped in `tutorialKey(...)` / `modalKey(...)` / `overlayKey(...)` / `bankingHintKey(...)` expressions. Editing wording therefore requires opening a `.ts` file, understanding the key syntax, and risking a compile error — which is a barrier for the non-developer content/editorial writer who owns the copy. The producer wants all tutorial copy in a **CSV file that can be opened and edited in a spreadsheet**.

## Users

- **Non-developer content/editorial writer** — owns tutorial wording; must be able to edit it in a spreadsheet without touching TypeScript.
- **Developer/maintainer** — must be able to trust that a spreadsheet save cannot silently break the tutorial (missing/orphan/duplicate keys, mangled quoting, dropped placeholders).
- **Player** — must see the same (correct, data-driven) tutorial copy as today; this change is behaviour-preserving.

### Example user stories

- As a content editor, I want to open one CSV, edit the `text` column in my spreadsheet, save it, and have the tutorial use my wording after the normal build, so that I never need to understand TypeScript.
- As a developer, I want a build-time/CI test that validates the CSV (keys, duplicates, placeholders, quoting) so that a bad spreadsheet save cannot ship broken tutorial copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **CSV is the single source of tutorial copy.** All tutorial strings — 26 step titles + 26 step bodies (`tutorial.T1..T26.title|body`), 4 offer-modal strings (`tutorial.modal.*`), 4 overlay button labels (`tutorial.overlay.*`), and 2 banking-hint strings (`tutorial.bankingHint.*`) — live in `src/i18n/tutorial-en.csv` with a `key,text` header. No user-facing prose string literals remain in `tutorial-en.ts` (it holds only key helpers + the loader). *Metric: a test asserts `tutorial-en.csv` has a `key,text` header and exactly the required keys; a grep/inspection confirms `tutorial-en.ts` contains no copy.*
2. **Loader preserves the public API.** `tutorial-en.ts` keeps exporting `TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE`, `TUTORIAL_I18N_KEY_PREFIX`, `tutorialKey`, `modalKey`, `overlayKey`, and `bankingHintKey`, and builds `TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE` from the CSV via a Vite `?raw` import + the core `parseCsv()` helper. All existing consumers (`src/TutorialFlow.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts`, tests) compile and pass **unchanged**. *Metric: existing `tutorial-i18n.test.ts`, `tutorial-text-updates.test.ts`, `tutorial-flow.test.ts` pass without edits.*
3. **CSV integrity is validated.** A test verifies: header is `key,text`; every required key is present; there are no duplicate or orphan/unknown keys; no value is empty; embedded commas round-trip; the embedded double quote in the banking hint (`"(1 banked)"`) round-trips; a leading UTF-8 BOM is tolerated (the loader strips it); and placeholder tokens (`{cardName}`, `{cost}`, `{bonus}`, `{synergyCardName}`) are preserved where expected. *Metric: `tests/main-street/tutorial-csv.test.ts` all green.*
4. **Behaviour is preserved end-to-end.** `resolveTutorialStepText()` and `t()` resolve the same content as before the migration for every step (including data-driven card facts from `card-data.csv` and the modal/overlay/banking labels), with no raw `{token}` text leaking. *Metric: existing content assertions plus a full required-key parity assertion pass.*
5. **Documentation reflects the spreadsheet workflow.** `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md` is updated so "Changing existing text" and "Adding a New Language" describe opening `tutorial-en.csv` in a spreadsheet, editing the `text` column, saving as CSV UTF-8 (quoting for embedded commas/quotes; keep placeholder tokens), and rebuilding. Any stale references to editing `tutorial-en.ts` are removed.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Bundle the CSV at build time via Vite `?raw` (no runtime `fetch`), matching `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts:13` (`./card-data.csv?raw`). A normal rebuild/redeploy is acceptable (producer Q3 = A).
- Use the existing core `parseCsv()` (`core/src/core-engine/CsvLoader.ts`, imported as `@core-engine/CsvLoader`) — no new runtime dependency. It already supports RFC4180 quoting: embedded commas, newlines, and escaped `""`.
- Preserve the i18n key scheme exactly (`tutorial.<STEP_ID>.<field>`, `tutorial.modal.*`, `tutorial.overlay.*`, `tutorial.bankingHint.*`).
- Preserve placeholder tokens `{cardName}` / `{cost}` / `{bonus}` / `{synergyCardName}`; card facts must keep resolving from `card-data.csv` at render time.
- Tolerate a UTF-8 BOM (`parseCsv` does not trim header cells, so the loader must strip it) and expect `parseCsv`'s value trimming.
- English only. No change to step order, gates, highlight zones, scenario, or gameplay logic.

## Existing state

- `src/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — `TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE: Record<string, string>` with inline strings plus key-helper functions and inline editorial comments.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts:88` — registers the bundle at module load (`registerLocale('en', TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE)`).
- `src/TutorialFlow.ts:68` — imports `bankingHintKey`/`tutorialKey`; steps carry only `titleKey`/`bodyKey`.
- `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md` — already documents the i18n architecture and says to edit `tutorial-en.ts`.
- Precedent for spreadsheet-editable bundled data: `card-data.csv` parsed by `parseCsv()` (`src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts`).
- Copy characteristics (measured at intake): 62 values; 13 contain commas; 1 contains an embedded double quote; none contain newlines.

## Desired change

Introduce `src/i18n/tutorial-en.csv` (`key,text`) holding all tutorial strings, and reduce `src/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` to a thin loader that imports the CSV `?raw`, parses it with `parseCsv()`, strips an optional BOM, and exports the same `TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE` plus key helpers. Add a CSV-integrity test and update the localization docs to describe the spreadsheet workflow.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/i18n/tutorial-en.csv` — **New.** `key,text` CSV holding all tutorial/modal/overlay/banking strings (spreadsheet-editable source of truth).
- `src/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — Convert to a thin loader: `?raw` import + `parseCsv()` + BOM strip → `TUTORIAL_EN_BUNDLE`; keep all existing exports.
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-csv.test.ts` — **New.** CSV integrity: header, required-key completeness, duplicates/orphans, empty values, comma/quote round-trip, BOM tolerance, placeholder preservation.
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-i18n.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tutorial-text-updates.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tutorial-flow.test.ts` — Confirm still pass unchanged (behaviour-preservation evidence).
- `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md` — Rewrite "Changing existing text" / "Adding a New Language" and the file-overview table for the CSV workflow.
- `docs/main-street/playtest-scenarios.md` — Update the tutorial-copy editing pointer.
- `core/src/core-engine/CsvLoader.ts` — Existing parser; use as-is (only touch if a proven gap, e.g. header trimming/BOM, is found).

## Related work

- **`CG-0MUAVHX1D002J8HH` — Easy editing of tutorial text (core store).** The originating item; this MS item mirrors it for the game repo that now owns the copy.
- **`MS-0MUN91YJ40092ZBM` — Steam follow CTA in the tutorial completion step** (open): later added the 5 `tutorial.steamFollow.*` keys to the CSV; the integrity test's required-key list grew from 62 to 67 accordingly.
- **`MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5` — Fix stale `example-games/main-street` paths in docs after the `src/` migration** (open): tracks the remaining stale path references in the localization docs.
- **`CG-0MP415DUV0032SKK` — Main Street tutorial localization and i18n externalization** (completed): externalised copy into the i18n bundle this item now moves to CSV.
- **`CG-0MS0IXWE2002ZQ16` / `CG-0MSBSCL0W005OALV` — Data-driven tutorial text** (completed): added `{cardName}`/`{cost}`/`{bonus}` placeholder resolution from `card-data.csv`; the CSV must preserve these tokens.
- **`CG-0MSBSCCPJ0050DT4` — Core i18n interpolation support** (completed): `t(key, params)` used during resolution.
- **`CG-0MSBSCRND009V8DS` / `CG-0MSLXJ1OK004LJKU` — Tutorial localization docs** (completed): docs this change revised again.
- **`CG-0MQK3IYDT0024SWG` — Tutorial text needs review on Main Street** (completed): editorial rules the CSV must continue to satisfy.
- **`CG-0MQF4A8QZ008NLWM` — Tests: Tutorial text updates** (completed): test suite guarding tutorial text content.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Spreadsheet round-trip mangling** (re-quoting, encoding, BOM, header changes) → mitigation: RFC4180 quoting is already supported; integrity test + BOM strip; docs instruct "Save As CSV (UTF-8)".
- **Silent key loss during migration** → mitigation: required-key parity test and unchanged existing content tests.
- **In-file editorial comments lost** in the move to CSV → mitigation: editorial rules live in `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md` and the loader's module comment (an optional `notes` column could be added later if writers want inline guidance).
- **`parseCsv` trims values and does not trim header cells** → assume no copy relies on leading/trailing whitespace (true at intake) and strip the BOM in the loader.
- **Scope creep** → do **not** extend this to `undo-challenge-en.ts`, add new locales, or build an in-game editor; record those as separate future work items.
- **Assumption:** a 2-column `key,text` layout is acceptable (a `notes`/`step` column can be added later without breaking the loader).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1** — "Is the existing `tutorial-en.ts` i18n bundle sufficient as the 'config file', or must copy move to a standalone data/config file?" (options: A close as satisfied / B standalone data file / C keep TS + tooling only). **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-26): "No not sufficient, we should use a CSV file that is editable in a spreadsheet."** → Chosen: **B**, CSV format.
- **Q2** — "Who is the intended editor of the tutorial text?" (A developer / B non-developer writer / C translator). **Answer (producer): "b (but does it matter?)"** → Non-developer content/editorial writer.
- **Q3** — "Does 'easy' require only no-code editing, or also no rebuild?" (A no-code + rebuild / B runtime fetch, no rebuild). **Answer (producer): "A"** → No-code editing plus a normal build/redeploy; the CSV is bundled via Vite `?raw`.

- **Automated CI/downtime worker** (herdr) that runs ruff and creates work items for lint findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Producer decides whether `tmp_` prefixed Python scripts should be exempt from EXE001 (i.e. whether this is a genuine false positive).

- Any ruff configuration change should be applied consistently to `core/ruff.toml`.
- The three related items are open and share the same rationale — they should be addressed together if a configuration change is warranted.

- `core/ruff.toml` excludes TypeScript/JavaScript files and ignores B018 for `.llm-wiki/` JSON files, but has no exclusion for EXE001 on `tmp_*.py` files.

Establish the shared test/verification foundation for the visual storyline
editor so every later feature can be driven test-first. This task writes
**test infrastructure only** — no editor feature code.

## Context

The editor is a dev tool launched under Vite/`vite-node`; the card model
imports `src/card-data.csv` through Vite's `?raw` query, so bridge tests must
run through the same toolchain. Repo test facts:

- `npm test` runs `vitest run --project unit` (Vitest; `tests/**/*.test.ts`,
  excluding `*.browser.test.ts`).
- Browser tests (`tests/**/*.browser.test.ts`) run through Vitest browser mode
  with the Playwright chromium provider (`@vitest/browser`, `playwright` are
  existing devDependencies) — project wiring lives with the launcher
  distribution, so a dev page (not a Phaser scene) needs explicit wiring.
- `ajv` is an existing devDependency and is used for JSON schema validation.
- The root `vite.config.ts` is **auto-generated** by
  `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`; do not hand-edit it — use a dedicated
  editor config file.

## Scope

- Fixture helper that copies `src/card-data.csv`,
  `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` and
  `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` into an isolated temp directory and
  returns the paths, so edit tests never mutate committed files.
- A reusable write-path guard helper: scans editor source files and asserts no
  module writes `src/card-data.csv` except through `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`
  (tolerant of editor modules not existing yet).
- A manifest schema guard test: committed manifest validates against
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` using `ajv`.
- A browser-test harness decision/spike: determine and wire how the editor dev
  page is driven in Vitest browser mode (or justify an alternative), with a
  placeholder test that passes. Record the decision in a comment on this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture helper returns isolated temp copies of the CSV/manifest/mmd, and a
  test asserts the committed originals are byte-identical afterwards.
- The write-path guard helper is exercised by a test and would fail if an
  editor module wrote the CSV directly (proven with a synthetic negative case).
- The committed manifest validates against the JSON schema in a unit test using
  the existing `ajv` devDependency.
- The browser-test path for a non-Phaser dev page is decided, wired and
  documented; a placeholder browser test passes without adding a runtime
  dependency.
- `npm test` and the browser suite run the new harness green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/fixtures.ts` — **new** temp-copy helper.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/fixtures.test.ts` — **new** helper test.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/write-path-guard.ts` — **new** reusable static guard.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/write-path-guard.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-editor/manifest-schema.test.ts` — **new** ajv guard.
- `vite.editor.config.ts` — **new** dedicated editor/harness config (not the auto-generated `./vite.config.ts`).

## Deliverables

- Fixture helper, write-path guard helper, schema guard test, decided + wired
  browser-test path, harness smoke coverage.

# Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player or observer, I want to watch AI-vs-AI competitive matches with spectator/replay visuals, so that I can study the AI strategies and enjoy demos without taking a turn.

## Background

- Discovered from epic **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** (Playable AI competitive mode). That epic covers the human-vs-AI playable mode; this item adds the all-AI observer experience on top and is **not** a dependency of the epic.
- The engine competitive mode and the selectable AI strategies (`Random`, `Greedy`, `BankingGreedy`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`) already exist (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`).
- Replay infrastructure exists: `src/scripts/adapters/MainStreetReplayAdapter.ts` (referenced by `configs/game.json`) and transcript recording via `recordMainStreetEvent` (`src/MainStreetTranscript.ts`).
- This item assumes the competitive UI from the epic exists (or an equivalent headless entry point) before it can be started.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AI-vs-AI match can be started.** A spectator can start a match where every seat is AI-controlled, choosing each AI's strategy/difficulty. *Metric: manual playthrough; all seats shown as AI with the chosen strategy.*
2. **Actions are visible as they happen.** Each AI action is presented in order (e.g. active-seat/turn indicator plus a transcript/log entry) so a spectator can follow the match. *Metric: visual verification of every AI action in a short match.*
3. **Deterministic replay.** A completed AI-vs-AI match can be replayed from its seed/transcript and yields the identical final state as the live run. *Metric: automated test replays a recorded match and asserts equality of the terminal state.*
4. **Playback controls.** The spectator can pause, resume, step and change playback speed. *Metric: manual verification of each control.*
5. **No regressions.** Single-player and the human-vs-AI competitive mode are unaffected. *Metric: existing unit/integration tests pass.*

## Notes

- Rendering/visual items may require manual verification; keep the deterministic-replay AC automated.
- Reuse the transcript/seed determinism already required by the engine rather than adding a parallel recording mechanism.

# Intake Brief: Avoid duplicate Main Street card SVG regeneration on game start (MS-0MUTU19SF007791K)

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Bug** | **Assignee: Map**

> Main Street regenerates all 174 card SVGs from CSV data twice on every game start, because `loadCampaignAndSetup()` regenerates synchronously and then regenerates again after the async static-SVG fetches resolve. The duplicate work wastes startup CPU and emits a misleading duplicate console log.

## Problem Statement

When a Main Street game starts, `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` runs twice, producing the duplicate console line:

```
MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts:112 [MainStreetSvgTextureManager] Regenerated 174 card SVGs from CSV data
MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts:112 [MainStreetSvgTextureManager] Regenerated 174 card SVGs from CSV data
```

The second regeneration exists as a defensive re-apply: `loadCardSvgSources()` (called from `preload()`) starts async `fetch()`es for the static SVG assets, and those fetch callbacks call `cardSvgSources.set(...)` unconditionally, so a late-resolving fetch can clobber the CSV-fresh SVG that the synchronous regeneration just produced. To defeat that race, `loadCampaignAndSetup()` chains a second `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` onto `cardSvgLoadPromise`.

That is correct but wasteful: the whole 174-row `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow()` pass (including embedded base64 card art) runs twice on every boot, and the duplicate log makes it look like the startup pipeline is broken. The same redundancy is latent in `checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()`, which regenerates a third time whenever a CSV mismatch is detected — even though the synchronous early regeneration has already made the sources fresh.

## Users

- **Developer:** Starting the dev server and reading the browser console. A duplicate "Regenerated 174 card SVGs" line is confusing and suggests the CSV/SVG startup pipeline is firing twice.
  - *"As a developer, I want the startup log to clearly show one regeneration, so I can trust that the CSV→SVG pipeline runs once and is not double-initialised."*
- **Player (startup latency):** Card SVG generation is on the boot critical path. Doing it twice adds avoidable work before the first frame renders.
  - *"As a player, I want the game to start as quickly as possible and not do redundant work while loading."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Single regeneration per CSV content per manager:** `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` is idempotent for an unchanged `CSV_CHECKSUM` — calling it twice in a row generates the CSV SVGs once, logs the "Regenerated … card SVGs" message once, and the second call is a cheap no-op. Verified by a unit test that spies on the generation pass / log and asserts one run.
2. **Fetched static SVGs never clobber CSV-fresh sources:** `loadCardSvgSources()` does not overwrite a `cardSvgSources` entry that is already populated, so a late-resolving static-SVG `fetch()` cannot replace a CSV-regenerated source. Verified by a unit test with a mocked `fetch` that pre-populates a template id and asserts it is unchanged after the fetch resolves.
3. **No regression in CSV freshness:** After the async `cardSvgLoadPromise` chain completes on a boot with unchanged CSV, every template id present in the CSV still maps to the CSV-generated SVG (not the static asset) and the non-CSV card-back template remains populated. Verified by an existing/added test.
4. **Redundant re-apply chain removed:** `loadCampaignAndSetup()` no longer performs a second `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` after `cardSvgLoadPromise`; the synchronous early regeneration remains, and prewarming is still guaranteed to run after a fresh regeneration. Verified by code inspection + the no-console-errors E2E remains green.
5. **Mismatch path is non-redundant:** When `checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()` runs against sources already regenerated for the current `CSV_CHECKSUM`, it does not trigger another full generation pass.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments (the JSDoc in `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` and the comments in `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts`), README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Preserve the CSV-freshness guarantee:** the fix must not reintroduce the race fixed by `CG-0MRH36Z6800065JC` (stale static SVGs winning over CSV data).
- **Keep the synchronous early regeneration:** it populates `cardSvgSources` before the async fetches resolve, so the first synchronous `refreshAll()` renders CSV-fresh cards rather than fallback placeholders. Removing it would regress first paint.
- **No new dependencies / no build-pipeline change:** work within the existing Vite + Phaser setup.
- **Game repo only:** this is a Main Street change (`tce-main-street`); no core-engine API changes are expected.

## Existing State

- `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` loops `getCsvRows()` and calls `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow(row)` for each row, storing results in `scene.cardSvgSources` and logging on success.
- `MainStreetSvgTextureManager.loadCardSvgSources()` fetches static SVGs (one per template id + the card back) and sets `cardSvgSources` unconditionally in each `.then()` callback.
- `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.loadCampaignAndSetup()` calls `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` synchronously and then reassigns `s.cardSvgLoadPromise = s.cardSvgLoadPromise.then(() => regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv())` — the source of the duplicate.
- `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()` may call `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` a third time.
- Existing unit tests in `tests/main-street/svg-texture-cache-invalidation.test.ts` cover regeneration + prewarm-at-DPR invalidation, but not idempotency or the fetch-overwrite guard.
- Background/design: `CG-0MRH36Z6800065JC` ("Ensure card data is loaded from CSV when a new game starts") introduced the synchronous early regeneration and documented the race; this item tidies the defensive double-regeneration it left behind.

## Desired Change

Make regeneration idempotent and remove the redundant re-apply:

1. **Track provenance for fetched vs regenerated sources.** In `loadCardSvgSources()`, only set a `cardSvgSources` entry when one is not already present (or otherwise record that CSV regeneration owns those keys), so static-SVG fetches can never overwrite CSV-fresh entries. The card-back template (not in the CSV) is still set by its fetch.
2. **Memoise CSV regeneration.** Record the `CSV_CHECKSUM` that `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` last generated for; a subsequent call with the same checksum returns early (no generation pass, no log). This makes the `checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()` path a no-op when sources are already fresh, and makes "Reset All Progress" (`StatsOverlay` re-invokes `loadCampaignAndSetup()`) cheap.
3. **Remove the redundant re-apply chain** in `loadCampaignAndSetup()`; keep the synchronous early regeneration and the existing `cardSvgLoadPromise.then(prewarm…)` ordering so prewarming still only sees fresh sources.
4. Update the surrounding comments/JSDoc to describe the new single-regeneration contract.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — Add CSV-checksum memoisation to `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` and a no-overwrite guard to `loadCardSvgSources()`; update JSDoc.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts` — Remove the second `regenerateSvgSourcesFromCsv()` re-apply chain in `loadCampaignAndSetup()`; update comments.
- `tests/main-street/svg-texture-cache-invalidation.test.ts` — Add unit tests for regeneration idempotency and the fetch no-overwrite guard.
- `tests/e2e/main-street-no-console-errors.browser.test.ts` — Existing guard that the boot pipeline stays console-clean; keep green (no change expected).

## Related Work

- `CG-0MRH36Z6800065JC` — [Completed] "Ensure card data is loaded from CSV when a new game starts". Introduced the synchronous early regeneration and the race-avoidance design that this item simplifies.
- `CG-0MRF343AJ004N6ZW` — [Completed] "Ensure SVGs are regenerated when CSV changes on game start and load". Added the CSV checksum + regeneration pipeline.
- `CG-0MRBDPFPH009Y8M0` — Game balance tooling built on CSV-driven card data (consumes the same `cardSvgSources`/regeneration seam).
- `MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY` — Canonical docs, cross-references & doc-drift guard (doc-relevant).

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

- **Stale-source regression:** if the no-overwrite guard is too broad, the card-back template or any template absent from the CSV could be left unpopulated. Mitigation: guard by presence of an existing entry only; do not filter by `ms_card_` prefix, and keep the guard template-agnostic so non-CSV assets still load.
- **Memoisation masking a legitimate re-generation.** If SVG generation ever becomes state-dependent (not purely CSV-derived), the checksum key would be insufficient. Mitigation: key the memo on `CSV_CHECKSUM` and document the invariant that generated SVGs are a pure function of the CSV.
- **Scene-restart map persistence:** `scene.cardSvgSources` is a scene-level `Map` that survives a scene restart; the memo lives on the (freshly constructed) manager. Mitigation: the synchronous regeneration still runs once per new manager and overwrites CSV keys, so restart remains correct.
- **Scope creep:** eliminating the static SVG fetch path entirely, or moving to runtime-only generation, is out of scope. Record such opportunities as linked work items.
- **Test brittleness:** asserting on `console.info` text is fragile. Prefer asserting on a spied generation call count / returned count, with the log check as a secondary assertion.

### Assumptions

- The two observed log lines come from the synchronous regeneration (`loadCampaignAndSetup`) plus the `cardSvgLoadPromise` re-apply, not from a second scene instance or the `StatsOverlay` "Reset All" path (that path is only reachable from the stats-confirm overlay).
- `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow()` output is a pure function of the CSV rows, so regeneration is safely memoised by `CSV_CHECKSUM`.
- The static SVGs are only a fallback for when CSV regeneration is unavailable/fails.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1: Is the duplicate regeneration a correctness bug or a performance/observability concern?**
  - Answer (operator, freeform seed): reported as a bug — the console output shows two identical regeneration lines. Analysis: the final rendered cards are correct (the defensive second pass wins); the impact is wasted startup work, a misleading log, and a fragile double-regeneration contract. Research: traced the two calls to `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.loadCampaignAndSetup()` (synchronous early call + `cardSvgLoadPromise` re-apply), with a latent third call in `checkForCsvMismatchAndRegenerate()`.
  - Final: treat as a medium-priority bug (redundant work + misleading observability), not a rendering-correctness failure.
- **Q2: Which repository/store should own this work?**
  - Answer (agent, per project multi-repo rules): the change is entirely within the sibling game repo `tce-main-street`, which has its own Worklog store (prefix `MS`), so the item is created there (`MS-0MUTU19SF007791K`). Historical related items live in the core `CG` store because Main Street was previously part of the core repo.
  - Final: Main Street store (`MS`).
- **Q3: Should the fix remove the static-SVG fetch path or just stop it clobbering regenerated sources?**
  - Answer (agent, scope control): out of scope. The minimal, robust change is to (a) prevent fetches from overwriting CSV-fresh entries and (b) memoise regeneration, leaving the static SVGs as the fallback path.
  - Final: keep the fetch/fallback path; only prevent overwrite and redundant regeneration.


## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** – Some staff cards should add action points (completed)
- **MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV** – Storyline model & extraction seam (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: again, async, avoid, boot, bug, calls, canvas, card, console, csv, data, defeat, dev, duplicate, fetch, game, line, main, observed, phaser, regeneration, renderer, report, scenes, see, seed, sequence, server, shown, src, start, street, svg, svgs, synchronously, via
- `core/docs/dev/test-suite-review.md` — matched: again, boot, bug, calls, canvas, card, console, csv, data, dev, duplicate, game, line, main, phaser, renderer, report, scenes, see, seed, sequence, server, src, start, street, svg, svgs, via

# Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player in competitive (human vs AI) mode, I want the score target reduced by 50% for each AI opponent, so that a competitive game against more AIs remains winnable in a comparable run length.

## Context

- The score target is `config.winThreshold` (single shared value): Easy 10000, Medium 12000, Hard 15000 (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`).
- The competitive first-to-threshold win check compares every player's per-owner score against that shared value (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`, `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`).
- The value is surfaced in the HUD (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`), help content (`src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts`), and used by AI look-ahead (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`).

## Producer decisions (confirmed)

- **Formula:** multiplicative — `effectiveWinThreshold = baseWinThreshold × 0.5 ^ N`, where `N` = number of AI opponents (e.g. 1 AI = 50%, 2 = 25%, 3 = 12.5%).
- **Scope:** the reduced value is **shared** — it is the target for all players in the competitive game (human and AI alike).
- **Endless mode:** applies to the **standard** win condition only (not an endless-mode continuation change).

## Scope

- **In:** derive the effective competitive win threshold from the seat configuration; use it consistently for the win check, AI look-ahead, and all player-facing score-target displays; tests.
- **Out:** changing single-player thresholds; changing the challenge/bankruptcy/reputation end conditions; rebalancing the base difficulty presets.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In a competitive game with `N` AI opponents, the effective win threshold used by the first-to-threshold win check equals `baseWinThreshold × 0.5^N`. *Metric: unit test over N = 1, 2, 3 asserting the value passed to the end-condition check and the winner declaration.*
2. The reduced threshold is shared by every player in that game (the same value governs the human and all AI seats). *Metric: integration test where the human and an AI each reach the effective threshold.*
3. Single-player is unchanged: the base `winThreshold` still applies. *Metric: existing single-player tests pass; explicit assertion of the unmodified value.*
4. All player-facing target displays (HUD score line, help text, any scoreboard) show the effective competitive threshold, not the base value. *Metric: rendering/unit tests assert the displayed target.*
5. AI look-ahead uses the effective threshold. *Metric: test asserting the AI horizon/distance computation uses the reduced value.*
6. A competitive game with `N` AI opponents resolves as a win when the first player reaches the effective threshold. *Metric: full-game integration test per N = 1..3.*
7. Save/load round-trips the effective threshold so a resumed competitive game keeps the reduced target. *Metric: serialise/deserialise test.*

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — derive/persist the effective competitive threshold at state creation.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — competitive end-condition check.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — AI look-ahead horizon.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`, `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — player-facing target display.
- `tests/main-street/` — unit + integration coverage.

## Dependencies and notes

- Discovered-from `MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP` (Playable AI competitive mode).
- Related balance item: `MS-0MUR9IMXE0090WIV` (Confirm win thresholds / run length as the difficulty lever).
- Reuse the existing seat-configuration model rather than duplicating opponent-count logic.

# Cross-owner business actions: seats can sell/close/upgrade businesses they do not own

## Problem statement

In competitive (human vs AI) play, the human seat can open the Manage-Card
dialog on an AI-owned street slot and **sell** or **close** that opponent's
business; the same ownership gap lets the human **upgrade** an opponent's
business. Each seat must only be able to mutate street slots it owns, in both
directions (human→AI and, defensively, AI→human).

## Users

- **Human player (competitive mode)** — expects opponent businesses to be
  untouchable; the current behaviour lets them destroy an opponent's engine and
  (for a sell) even credits the acting seat's wallet.
- **AI opponents** — must be prevented from mutating the human's businesses;
  today they emit no sell/close actions, but no guard exists to stop a future
  AI upgrade/sell/close path from doing so.

Example user stories:

- As a competitive player, I want to be unable to sell or close a business I
  do not own, so that opponents' engines are protected and the game is fair.
- As a competitive player, I want clear feedback when I click a slot I do not
  own, so that I understand why the action is unavailable.
- As a game designer, I want ownership enforced in one legality layer, so that
  UI, AI, and headless paths cannot diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive mode, `canSellBusiness`/`sellBusiness` reject a slot whose
   owner (`getSlotOwnerId`) is not the acting seat (`state.activePlayerId`),
   returning a `LegalityResult` with a clear reason; the action mutates no
   state. Single-player (no `ownerTaggedGrid`) behaviour is unchanged.
2. In competitive mode, `canCloseBusiness`/`closeBusiness` reject a slot whose
   owner is not the acting seat with the same guarantees; a rejected close
   consumes no action.
3. In competitive mode, upgrade actions (`canPurchaseUpgrade`,
   `canPlayUpgradeFromHand`, and their execution paths) reject targeting an
   opponent-owned business; eligible-target search does not select an
   opponent-owned slot as the default target.
4. Clicking a non-owned occupied slot in the scene blocks the Manage-Card
   dialog and shows illegal-move feedback with an ownership-specific message
   (e.g. "That business belongs to AI 1."); no dialog is opened and no Sell /
   Close / upgrade command runs.
5. Any coins from a permitted sell are credited to the owning seat's wallet
   (not an unrelated seat), and a permitted close leaves the slot immediately
   placeable by its owner; both behaviours are covered by tests.
6. Tests cover: human cannot sell/close/upgrade an AI-owned business; a seat
   can sell/close its **own** business (positive case); single-player
   sell/close/upgrade is unaffected; and the legality helpers return the
   expected reasons.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Enforce at the legality/command layer** (operator decision Q3 = A), not the
  scene layer alone, so UI, AI and headless paths share one source of truth.
- **Preserve single-player behaviour**: single-player states have no
  `ownerTaggedGrid`; the gate must be a no-op there.
- **Reuse existing ownership primitives**: `getSlotOwnerId`
  (`MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`), `ownerTaggedGrid`, `activePlayerId`.
- **No new scoring/economy rules**: this is an access-control fix, not a
  balance change.
- **Headless/Monte-Carlo determinism** must not change for existing seeds where
  neither seat acted cross-owner (the AI emits no such actions today).
- Do not weaken the existing phase, sold-slot, action-budget, or placement-mode
  gates already in `canSellBusiness`/`canCloseBusiness`.

## Existing state

- `canSellBusiness`, `sellBusiness`, `canCloseBusiness`, `closeBusiness`
  (`src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`) contain **no ownership check**.
- `sellBusiness` credits `state.resourceBank.coins` directly, with no per-owner
  routing.
- `onSellCard` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts`) opens the
  Manage-Card dialog for any occupied, non-sold slot in `market` phase.
- `showSellConfirmation` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`) wires Sell
  and Close buttons that execute with no ownership check.
- `canPurchaseUpgrade` / `canPlayUpgradeFromHand` / `purchaseUpgrade`
  (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`) have no ownership check;
  `findTargetBusinessSlot` may resolve to an opponent-owned business.
- Ownership is modelled: `getSlotOwnerId`, `tagSlotOwnerIfCompetitive`
  (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`), `ownerTaggedGrid`, `activePlayerId`,
  and `PlayerRecord.controller` (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`).
- The AI action enumerator (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
  `enumerateLegalActions`) emits no sell/close actions today; competitive
  income/costs are already routed per owner via `getSlotOwnerId`.

## Desired change

- Add an ownership guard to the sell/close legality and execution functions:
  when `ownerTaggedGrid` is present, require
  `getSlotOwnerId(state, slotIndex) === (state.activePlayerId ?? 0)`; otherwise
  reject with a descriptive reason. Single-player remains a no-op.
- Apply the same guard to upgrade targeting (`canPurchaseUpgrade`,
  `canPlayUpgradeFromHand`, and execution), and ensure default target selection
  never picks an opponent-owned slot.
- Gate the scene path (`onSellCard`) and/or the overlay so a non-owned slot
  cannot open the Manage-Card dialog; show the ownership-specific illegal-move
  message instead.
- Ensure a permitted sell credits the owning seat's wallet (the acting seat is
  the owner once the guard is in place — verify no separate routing is needed).
- Add focused unit tests plus a browser/scene-level test for the blocked dialog.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts` — add ownership gate to `canSellBusiness`,
  `sellBusiness`, `canCloseBusiness`, `closeBusiness`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — add ownership gate to
  `canPurchaseUpgrade`, `canPlayUpgradeFromHand`, `purchaseUpgrade`; fix
  `findTargetBusinessSlot` default selection.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — reuse `getSlotOwnerId`; may add a small
  `canActOnOwner`/`isSlotOwnedByActiveSeat` helper.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — apply the same guard to the legacy
  `sellFromTableau` / `canSellFromTableau` path if still reachable.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts` — block `onSellCard` for
  non-owned slots with ownership feedback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — defensive guard in the Sell/Close
  handlers (and hide/disable when non-owned).
- `tests/main-street/CloseBusiness.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/MainStreetSellCards.test.ts` — extend with ownership cases.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-*.test.ts` — add cross-owner sell/close/upgrade
  cases (a new `competitive-ownership-actions.test.ts` is likely cleanest).
- `tests/main-street/manage-card-dialog.browser.test.ts` — blocked-dialog case.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUUDWIXG009IB0W` — Reject illegal moves before animation and
  action-point deduction (completed; the established pattern for validating a
  move before any state mutation/animation — reuse it for the ownership gate).
- `MS-0MT5X3GMA007EG30` — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the
  shared street (epic, establishes `ownerTaggedGrid`).

# Intake Brief: Level-2 Upgrade Prerequisite Gate Blocks Expensive-Tier Adoption

**Work item:** MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 · `task` · `high`
**Discovered from:** MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M (Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance)
**Producer decisions:** Q1→(a), Q2→(a), Q3→(a) — see Appendix.

## Headline

On the canonical greedy Monte Carlo profile (200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, Medium) four level-2 upgrades — `upg-grand-bakehouse`, `upg-restaurant`, `upg-multiplex`, `upg-luxury-retreat` — still sit at **0% M1 pick rate** and **0% M5 adoption**, because the AI almost never advances their parent businesses to level 1. This item re-tunes the *level-1 prerequisite cards'* `cost` values (card-data only) so the level-2 tier becomes reachable through the intended two-step chain, while leaving the level gate itself (US-19) intact.

## Problem statement

Level-2 upgrades are structurally gated: the AI emits a `buy-upgrade` action only when a business satisfies `biz.name === card.targetBusiness && biz.level === requiredLevel && biz.level < biz.maxLevel` (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`). The four level-2 upgrades carry `requiredLevel: 1`, so they need a parent already at level 1. The greedy AI advances only ~7–13% of parents to level 1, so the intersection of *(level-2 card in market) × (parent at level 1) × (affordable)* is effectively zero. Cost/`incomeBonus` changes on the level-2 cards themselves cannot move adoption (Experiment B preserved 0% M1), because the binding constraint is upstream: too few level-1 parents exist.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the late-game investment tier to be a real choice (e.g. "My Diner is doing well — should I push it to a full Restaurant?"). Today the most powerful upgrades in the pool are unreachable in practice.
- **Producer / designer** — wants the level-2 chain to function as designed (a two-step progression reward) and to be demonstrably reachable in the canonical simulation, without weakening the chain design.
- **Developer** — wants a small, reversible card-data change with before/after Monte Carlo evidence, consistent with the parent item's card-data-only precedent.

User story: *As a player running a profitable Bakery, I want a path to the Grand Bakehouse to be realistically attainable, so that investing in a favourite business pays off over a full run.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Baseline and before/after evidence captured.** On the canonical profile (200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, `greedy`, sweep Easy/Medium/Hard — command below), record M1 pick rate for the four level-2 upgrades and M5 adoption for the four parents (Bakery, Diner, Cinema, Day Spa) and their level-1 prerequisites, both before and after the change, commit-stamped in the work-item description.
2. **Target reachable.** All four level-2 upgrades reach **≥5% M1** on the canonical Medium profile, with a non-zero absolute purchase count.
3. **Leading indicator rises.** Level-1 parent adoption (M5 for `upg-patisserie`/`upg-bread-factory`, `upg-bistro`/`upg-fast-food`, `upg-imax`/`upg-drive-in`, `upg-resort-spa`/`upg-wellness-center`) measurably increases versus the captured baseline.
4. **Gate and chain preserved.** The four level-2 upgrades keep `requiredLevel: 1`, and `canPurchaseUpgrade()` still enforces level equality (PRD-milestone-2 US-19 AC2/AC3 unchanged). No engine-rule changes in this item.
5. **Ladder preserved.** Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard win-rate ordering is retained and the Medium win-rate moves within ±0.05 of the pre-change baseline.
6. **Testing and validation.** A Vitest test asserts the canonical card-data invariant (the four level-2 upgrades have `requiredLevel: 1`) and the M1/M5 metric computation used for the before/after evidence; the full project test suite passes with the new values.
7. **Documentation.** `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` are updated where the re-derived costs are referenced; code comments touched by the change are updated.

## Constraints

- **Card-data values only** (`src/card-data.csv`, and only `cost` / `incomeBonus` fields). No engine-rule, AI-priority, or deck-mechanic changes in this item.
- **Preserve US-19** (`docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md`): level-2 upgrades keep `requiredLevel: 1`; `canPurchaseUpgrade()` equality is unchanged; the two-step chain described in `card-catalog.md` remains valid.
- **If the ≥5% target is unreachable** within card-data-only tuning, raise a **separate** engine/deck work item (e.g. a per-card market weight/copies column or a shared upgrade-deck `copies` change) rather than expanding this item's scope.
- Adjustments must be minimal and reversible, with commit-stamped before/after evidence.
- Win-rate ladder Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard must be preserved.
- No CHANGELOG.md edits (managed by the ship/release pipeline).

## Existing state

Canonical profile: 200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, greedy, Medium (current `dev` tip). Six upgrades at **0% M1 / 0% M5**:

| Upgrade | Level req. | Parent | Card `cost` | Outcome |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| `upg-museum` | 0 | Art Gallery (rare) | 700 | 0% M1 |
| `upg-dental-clinic` | 0 | Dentist (rare) | 700 | 0% (7.1% when cost→300) |
| `upg-grand-bakehouse` | 1 | Bakery | 900 | 0% M1 |
| `upg-restaurant` | 1 | Diner | 1400 | 0% M1 |
| `upg-multiplex` | 1 | Cinema | 1400 | 0% M1 |
| `upg-luxury-retreat` | 1 | Day Spa | 1400 | 0% M1 |

Parent purchase counts across 200 runs: Bakery 44, Diner 38, Cinema 34, Day Spa 7. Level-1 parents (of 200): Bakery ~4, Diner ~8, Cinema ~4, Day Spa ~4.

Prior experiments (recorded on the work item): removing the gate lifts the four level-2 upgrades to 2.9–10.3% M1 (isolates the gate); aggressive level-2 cost/bonus cuts leave them at 0% M1; boosting level-1 prerequisite `incomeBonus` barely moves level-1 adoption because the AI's Priority-3 upgrade purchase is unconditional; lowering `upg-dental-clinic` cost 700→300 alone reached 7.1% M1. **Cost (affordability) is the only score-independent card-data lever not yet fully tested.**

Reproduce the baseline:

```bash
npx vite-node src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts \
  --sweep --seeds 200 --seed-prefix mc-balance --maxTurns 60 \
  --sweep-strategies greedy --sweep-difficulties Easy,Medium,Hard \
  --out results/level2-gate-before.json
```

M1/M5 are derived from `MonteCarloRunSummary.marketOffers` / `cardsOwned` via the balance-analysis API (`computePickRate`, `computeUpgradeAdoption`; see `docs/main-street/balance-analysis-api.md`).

## Desired change

Re-tune the **level-1 prerequisite cards'** `cost` values down (and their `incomeBonus` only where cost alone is insufficient) so that materially more parents reach level 1, and, if required, reduce the level-2 cards' `cost` so an existing level-1 parent can afford the second step. The gate stays in place; the chain is preserved. Concretely, candidates are the expensive level-1 branches — `upg-bread-factory` (700), `upg-fast-food` (700), `upg-imax` (700), `upg-drive-in` (700), `upg-wellness-center` (900), `upg-resort-spa` (900) — plus the level-2 `cost`s (`upg-grand-bakehouse` 900; `upg-restaurant`/`upg-multiplex`/`upg-luxury-retreat` 1400). Evidence must show which lever did the work.

If card-data tuning proves insufficient to reach ≥5% M1, document the shortfall and create the follow-up engine/deck work item; do not change engine rules here.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — adjust `cost` (and `incomeBonus` where justified) for the six level-1 prerequisite cards and, if needed, the four level-2 cards; do **not** change `requiredLevel`.
- `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts` — canonical profile runner (sweep mode, `mc-balance` seeds, 60 turns).
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — run loop; source of `marketOffers` / `cardsOwned` per-card metrics.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `buy-upgrade` action generation (level-gate matching) and Priority-2/3 selection; read-only reference for the gate semantics.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — `canPurchaseUpgrade()` and the level/`displayName` mutation on upgrade application.
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — US-19 (Multi-Level Upgrade Chains) constraint; read-only.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — multi-level upgrade chain description and cost references.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — upgrade cost formula used to re-derive values.
- `core/src/balance-cards/` — balance cost-curve helpers (used by `run-balance-cards`), if re-derivation uses them.
- `tests/main-street/balance-cards.test.ts` — existing balance-card tests; extend for the invariant test.
- `src/scripts/balance/baseline-blocks.ts` — baseline/target blocks used by guardrail checks.

## Related work

- MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M — Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance (source item; `blocked`, card-data-only precedent).
- MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3 — Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns and economy re-tune (completed; introduced the payback regime).
- MS-0MUQUBK1B006EODZ — After-state Monte Carlo, guardrails and baseline (completed; canonical profile definition).
- MS-0MUQUBJQF009PTZ0 — Re-tune compensating balance levers (completed).
- MS-0MUVPB1UE004UUBI / MS-0MUUYI950004TG7F — upgrade ownership/regression tests (completed; test precedent).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** – Playable AI competitive mode (human vs AI) (completed)
- **MS-0MUML5X1L008LT8Z** – Implement Physiotherapist rename across all files (completed)
- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** – Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the docs build (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, action, affordable, alone, already (+134 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, action, alone, already, bakehouse (+117 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: action, adoption, affordable, alone, already (+115 more)

> The keyword matches above are low-precision (shared vocabulary); the manual **Related work** list is the authoritative set. Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4.md`.

## Assumptions

- The M1/M5 formulas and canonical profile remain stable; comparisons are like-for-like at the same seed/strategy/difficulty.
- The greedy AI's unconditional Priority-3 upgrade purchase is unchanged (no AI edits in scope), so affordability and market co-occurrence are the operative levers.
- `200 seeds` gives adequate resolution for a ≥5% target (5% ≈ 1.5 purchases of ~30 appearances; small-n noise is acknowledged and the leading indicator plus absolute counts are reported alongside).

## Risks

- **Small-n noise**: M1 on ~30 appearances is coarse; a ≥5% target could pass/fail by chance. *Mitigation:* report absolute purchase counts and the level-1 leading indicator; consider a larger seed count for the decisive run.
- **Card-data tuning insufficient**: if level-1 adoption cannot be lifted enough without an engine/deck change, the ≥5% target may be unreachable in scope. *Mitigation:* explicit escalation path to a separate engine work item (documented, not silent scope creep).
- **Ladder regression**: cheaper upgrades may shift win rates. *Mitigation:* AC4 ladder check with the ±0.05 Medium band.
- **Scope creep**: other zero-adoption cards (`upg-museum`, `upg-dental-clinic` with rare parents) invite broadening. *Mitigation:* keep them out of scope; log as separate work if needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (fix direction, given US-19).** Which approach should this item implement? — **Answer (operator): (a)** Preserve US-19 and the two-step chain; lift level-2 reachability by re-tuning level-1 prerequisite costs (card-data-only, matching the parent's "cost + incomeBonus only" scope); escalate to an engine/deck change as a separate work item only if the ≥5% target is unreachable. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (acceptance criteria).** Keep the proposed targets *plus* a level-1 leading-indicator AC? — **Answer (operator): (a)** Yes — keep the proposed ACs and add the level-1 leading indicator. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (scope boundary).** Card-data values only, or allow a minimal engine/deck change in this item? — **Answer (operator): (a)** Card-data values only first; spin off any engine change as a new work item. Source: interactive reply.

Research note (agent): `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` US-19 AC2/AC3 require `requiredLevel: 1` and `canPurchaseUpgrade()` level equality; the original "Experiment A" (`requiredLevel 1→0`) would break a committed PRD AC and the chain, so option (a) was adopted. Experiment C's null result is explained by the AI's unconditional Priority-3 purchase, which makes `incomeBonus` score-independent and leaves `cost` (affordability) as the viable card-data lever.

# Piggyback on other players' organiser actions

## Problem statement

In competitive (human vs AI) play, when one player organises a town-wide event such as a Local Festival, the benefits are currently routed only to that acting player's own wallet (`applyCompetitiveEventEffects`). There is no way for the other player(s) to participate in, or benefit from, an event that thematically belongs to the whole town. This makes events feel private rather than communal and removes a legible, interesting per-event decision from the non-acting player.

## Users

Primary user: the **human player in competitive mode**, who wants a meaningful reactive decision when the AI organises a town event.

- As the human player, when the AI organises a festival, I want to choose whether to co-fund it so that I can earn the full reward, or simply enjoy the spill-over benefit for free.
- As the human player, I want the trade-off to be explicit (coins and action cost vs. reward share) so the decision is legible.
- Secondary user: the **AI seat**, which needs a deterministic policy for the same decision so headless Monte Carlo runs stay reproducible.

## Proposed mechanic (design summary)

When a player plays a **piggyback-eligible Investment event** (an "organiser" event — e.g. Local Festival, Harvest Festival) during their MarketPhase, every **other active player** receives a 50% share of that event's rewards **automatically**, and is offered the single choice to **join fully**:

| Option | Cost | Reward |
|--------|------|--------|
| **Join fully** | **150% of the cost the acting player paid for the event** (paid from the piggybacker's own coins); **no action point is spent** | **100%** of the event's rewards |
| **Free-ride (automatic default)** | Nothing | **50%** of the event's rewards, granted automatically |

- The free-ride 50% is always applied, so there is **no "decline everything" option** and no prompt to refuse it — the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade 50% → 100%.
- Joining fully does **not** consume an action point; the seed's "take an additional action" means the player participates in the event (an additional participant), not that a budget action is spent.
- Rewards (coin + reputation) are computed on the **piggybacker's own board**, consistent with the existing per-owner event routing (`SpecificSynergy` rewards count the owner's own matching businesses), then scaled to 100% (join fully) or 50% (free-ride).
- The cost baseline is the amount the acting player **actually paid** for the event (after any cost discounts the acting player holds), not necessarily the card's nominal listed cost.
- If the piggybacker cannot afford 150% of that cost, the join-fully option is unavailable and the 50% free-ride applies.
- The acting player's own reward, and the shared market/incident deck, are unaffected by piggyback decisions.
- The mechanic applies **only in competitive mode (N≥2)**; single-player (N=1) has no other players and is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Eligibility & trigger.** When an active player plays a piggyback-eligible **organiser** Investment event during their MarketPhase in competitive mode (N≥2), every other non-eliminated player automatically receives the 50% free-ride share and is offered the join-fully upgrade for that event; playing a non-eligible event (or any event in N=1) produces no share and no prompt. Verified by unit tests over a flagged eligible card and an unflagged card.
- [ ] **AC2 — Join-fully tier.** Choosing "join fully" deducts exactly 150% of the cost the acting player paid for the event from the piggybacker's own coin balance (and **no action point**), then credits the piggybacker 100% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board). The option is unavailable (and never partially charged) when the piggybacker cannot afford the cost. Verified by unit tests asserting exact before/after coin and reputation values and an unchanged action budget.
- [ ] **AC3 — Free-ride tier.** Every non-acting eligible player automatically receives 50% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board) with no prompt to decline, spending no action point and no coins. This is also the fallback when "join fully" is unaffordable. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Isolation, determinism & persistence.** The acting player's reward and all shared decks are byte-for-byte unchanged by piggyback decisions; decisions for N>2 are resolved independently per seat in a deterministic order with no additional RNG draws; a pending piggyback decision survives a save/load round-trip. Verified by tests (including a replay/equality check and a serialize→deserialize→resolve test).
- [ ] **AC5 — AI policy and human prompt.** AI seats decide whether to join fully via a deterministic strategy heuristic in `MainStreetAiStrategy`; the human seat is offered the choice to join fully (pay the cost for 100%) or keep the automatic 50% free-ride, through the existing choice/prompt plumbing. Verified by an AI-policy unit test and a scene/command-layer test for the human prompt.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md`, and any relevant PRD/scope notes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Tests.** New unit tests cover eligibility, both tiers, the unaffordable fallback, N>2 isolation, AI policy and save/load; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation and economy scale.** Costs in this game are large (Local Festival lists at 300 coins; Harvest Festival and similar events are comparable). 150% of a 300-coin event is 450 — a significant sink — so the AI heuristic and the human prompt must state the exact coin cost and the resulting reward share.
- **Determinism.** Competitive mode is exercised by a headless Monte Carlo harness and deterministic replay/transcript tests; the mechanic must not introduce additional RNG draws in the resolution path.
- **Per-owner authority.** `PlayerRecord.coins` / `.reputation` are authoritative in competitive mode (the shared `resourceBank` is a scratch mirror). Piggyback cost and reward must mutate the piggybacker's `PlayerRecord`, not the shared wallet.
- **Backwards compatibility.** Adding a per-card eligibility flag must default to "not eligible" so existing card data and save files are unaffected; older saves without the pending-piggyback field must load with a null default.
- **Turn terminology.** Use canonical "turn"/"week" vocabulary; player-facing text is guarded by `scripts/check-terminology-guards.sh`.

## Existing state

- Competitive mode (N players on one owner-tagged street, alternating MarketPhases within a shared day) is implemented engine-side. `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` orchestrates the shared day; `endCompetitiveMarketTurn` round-robins seats.
- Investment events are played during the acting seat's MarketPhase via `playEventFromHand` (`MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`) and dispatchers in `MainStreetEngineActions.ts` (`buy-event`, `play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`).
- `applyCompetitiveEventEffects` (`MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`) already routes an Investment event's deltas to the **acting player only** (`actingId`), and computes `SpecificSynergy` rewards per owner from that owner's matching businesses. This is the natural seam for a scaled (100%/50%) piggyback reward.
- Per-card data lives in `src/card-data.csv` with an extensive column set; event rows currently carry `trigger`, `effect`, `target`, `targetSynergy`, `coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`, `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, etc. There is **no** piggyback/eligibility column yet.
- A precedent for deferring a player decision already exists: dual-choice incidents stash `state.pendingEventChoice` and pause the turn with `TurnResult.choicePending`, then resolve via `resolveEventChoice` / `resolveEventOption`; the pending choice is serialized in `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The piggyback decision should reuse this "pending decision + pause/resume" pattern.
- AI action enumeration and scoring live in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`; there is no piggyback decision yet, and no repo occurrence of "piggyback" anywhere.
- Actions are budgeted per seat (`PlayerRecord.actionBudget`) and partly bankable (`state.bankedActions`, capped at 2). Piggybacking does **not** spend an action point; the acting player's normal action consumption is unchanged.

## Desired change

- Add a per-card **piggyback-eligibility** flag (CSV column + `EventCard` field) defaulting to false, and mark organiser events such as Local Festival / Harvest Festival as eligible.
- When an eligible event is played in competitive mode, raise a **pending piggyback decision** for each other active player; pause/resume the shared day using the existing pending-choice pattern so the acting player's resolution completes first.
- Apply the chosen tier: join fully = −150% of the cost the acting player paid, +100% rewards (no action cost); free-ride = +50% rewards, applied automatically. Rewards are computed from the piggybacker's own board via the existing per-owner event math (then scaled).
- Add a deterministic **AI join-fully policy** and a **human prompt** offering join-fully vs. keep-50% (no decline option).
- Serialize/deserialize the pending decision; keep older saves loading.
- Update docs, code comments and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `piggybackable` column; mark organiser event rows (Local Festival, Harvest Festival, …) as eligible.
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` / `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — parse and expose the eligibility flag on `EventCard`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — `playEventFromHand` / `playHeldEvent` hook that raises piggyback opportunities after the acting player's event resolves.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — reward computation seam: scale and route event rewards to a piggybacker's own wallet.
- `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts` — cover both event-play dispatch paths (`play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`); new piggyback `PlayerAction` variants if needed.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — pending-piggyback state machine, pause/resume of the shared day.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` / `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — pending-piggyback state shape and action/result types.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` / `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — persist the pending decision with a null default for older saves.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — deterministic AI piggyback decision policy.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` (+ overlay/HUD renderers) — human prompt for the decision.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — document the mechanic, tiers and AI policy.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — competitive-only scope.** The mechanic applies only when N≥2; single-player has no other player to piggyback on. Revisit only if a solo "friendly town" flavour is later wanted.
- **Confirmed — free-ride is automatic.** Per the producer, the 50% free-ride is always applied and never offered as a decline option; the only player decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%.
- **Confirmed — no action-point cost.** Joining fully spends coins only (150% of the acting player's paid cost); the action budget is untouched.
- **Risk — economy runaway.** Stacking 100%-reward participation across many organiser events could inflate a seat's economy. Mitigation: the 150% cost premium; re-run the competitive Monte Carlo harness and record before/after win-rate/score attribution.
- **Risk — turn-resume complexity.** Pausing the shared day to await a piggyback decision touches the same deferred-closing machinery as dual-choice incidents. Mitigation: reuse the `pendingEventChoice` pattern and cover pause/resume + save/load with dedicated tests (AC4/AC5).
- **Risk — AI legality.** The AI must never attempt the full tier without the action or coins. Mitigation: share one affordability predicate between the eligibility gate and the AI policy, tested directly.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Extending piggybacking to business purchases/upgrades/staff hires is out of scope unless Q1 selects option (c); record any such desire as a separate linked work item rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- `MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ` — *Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution* (feature, completed) — establishes the per-owner event routing this mechanic builds on.
- `MS-0MT5X3GMA007EG30` — *Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street* (epic, done) — the competitive engine this mechanic extends.
- `MS-0MTSHG8RP008E128` — dual-choice incident deferred-resolution pattern (referenced in code comments; the save/load and pause/resume precedent to reuse).
- `MS-0MUVUPWHD0032CU4` — *Turns do not bank when playing against AI* (completed) — action-budget/banking rules a piggyback action must respect.
- `MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2` — *AI seat elimination with business closure* (completed) — defines "other active players" (non-eliminated seats only).
- `MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5` — *Re-price community spaces and events…* (completed) — the event cost/reward baseline used by the 150%/100%/50% maths.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed intent was clear on the headline rule but left several design details open. All questions below were answered by the producer on 2026-10-07; the confirmed answers are recorded inline and the brief has been updated to match.

- **Q1 — Which actions are piggyback-eligible?** — Answer (producer): **organiser events only** (option a) — a per-card opt-in flag on Investment "organiser" events (festivals, fairs, community gatherings); not all Investment events and not purchases/upgrades/staff hires. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q2 — What does "take an additional action" mean, and is the 50% tier a choice?** — Answer (producer): joining fully **does not cost an action point**; it costs **150% of the cost paid by the original (acting) player**. There is no point in declining the 50% free-ride, so **no decline option is offered** — the 50% share is automatic and the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q3 — Reward and cost baseline for the piggybacker.** — Answer (producer): **confirm** — rewards are the event's deltas computed on the **piggybacker's own board** (per-owner `SpecificSynergy` matching), scaled ×1.0 (join fully) / ×0.5 (free-ride); the cost is 150% of the cost the acting player paid (per Q2). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q4 — Multi-player prompt ordering and simultaneous decisions.** — Answer (producer): **as recommended** — decisions are solicited and resolved one seat at a time in seat order, independently per seat, before the shared day continues. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.

Discovered from MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 (Level-2 upgrade prerequisite gate blocks expensive-tier adoption in greedy Monte Carlo).

## Goal

Make the four level-2 capstone upgrades reachable in the canonical greedy Monte Carlo profile by changing **upgrade-deck composition / market weighting**, not card stats.

## Why (evidence from MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4)

Card-data-only cost tuning (level-1 prerequisites 700→400/900→500; level-2 900/1400/1400/1400→700/1000/1000/1000) left the four capstones at ~0–2.8% M1 on greedy/Medium/200 seeds. An even more aggressive variant (level-1 cost 200, level-2 cost 400) produced **identical** adoption, proving cost/affordability is not the binding constraint.

The binding constraint is co-occurrence: a capstone can only be bought when a parent business is already at level 1 AND the capstone card is in the market — but the market shows at most **one upgrade per turn** drawn from a 78-card upgrade deck (39 templates × 2 copies). Across 200 runs only 0–1 runs had both a level-1 parent and the matching capstone on offer.

## Proposed levers (pick one, measure with before/after Monte Carlo)

1. Increase the upgrade-deck copies for the four capstone templates (e.g. 2 → 4) and/or their level-1 prerequisite branches.
2. Add a per-card market weight / draw-weight column so chain cards appear more often than generic upgrades.
3. Reserve one market upgrade slot for chain-relevant upgrades when a matching parent exists at the required level.

Any option must preserve US-19 (`requiredLevel: 1`, `canPurchaseUpgrade()` level equality), the Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard ladder, and the ±0.05 Medium win-rate band.

## Acceptance criteria

1. All four level-2 capstones (upg-grand-bakehouse, upg-restaurant, upg-multiplex, upg-luxury-retreat) reach **≥5% M1** on the canonical greedy/Medium profile (200 seeds, prefix mc-balance, 60 turns), with before/after evidence commit-stamped.
2. Level-1 prerequisite adoption measurably rises vs the MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 after-state.
3. US-19 level gate and two-step chain preserved; no card-stat-only change.
4. Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard ladder preserved; Medium win-rate within ±0.05 of the pre-change baseline.
5. Tests cover the new deck/weight rule; full suite green.

- src/MainStreetCardsDecks.ts (createUpgradeDeck copies / weights)
- src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts / MainStreetStateSetup.ts (market draw)
- src/card-data.csv (only if a weight column is added)

- docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md — US-19.
